title: [_native][4/8] Serve narrow rows on the tile body, TMA-staged where that wins
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.18.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #195062
* #195061
* #195059
* #195051
* __->__ #195056
* #195052
* #195050
* #195049

Human Notes:

Optimization for tall-and-narrow reductions - large M, small N. Potentially use TMA
for these cases where that has been measured to be faster.

Codex:

Add a one-thread-per-row configuration for tall, narrow reductions, avoiding
the idle lanes imposed by a full-warp row mapping. For wider narrow rows, TMA
stages whole rows into shared memory and rotates reads to avoid bank
conflicts.

The measured row-count and chunk gates retain direct loads where they are
faster. TMA additionally requires SM90+, fp32, a power-of-two row length, and
a lane stride at the measured direct-load cliff. The shared body validates
those requirements even when callers force the option.

Test Plan:

```
spin quicklint
python test/python_native/test_kernel_rowtile.py
```

Authored with assistance from an AI coding agent.

items.author: slayton58
items.body:
Claude review response:
* Po2 precondition: Added
* shmem > 48KB gating -- cuteDSL will automagically request extra shmem for larger-capacity kernels, and some of the fastest are 64KB. The only requirement is less than the per-arch max shmem, but even that is a noisy failure, so I'm comfortable leaving it -- it should never happen, but is clear when it does.
* Test coverage -- added test(s) for the routing arm
